title: The Fire Captain's Stone in Helsinki, Finland

article.title: The Fire Captain's Stone in Helsinki, Finland
article.summary: In the courtyard of central Helsinki's oldest surviving wooden house, a rough-hewn cube of reddish granite sits low in the gravel, flat-topped enough to double as a seat. For decades it was the favorite perch of Alexander Wickholm, the fire captain ( ruiskumestari , literally "hose master"), who liked to smoke his pipe there while keeping an eye on the yard. Wickholm died in 1896. Nearly three decades later, in 1923, his granddaughter Martta had the stone moved near his grave at a cemetery across town. Almost immediately, the house began to misbehave. Tenants reported banging on the attic stairs and shutters that slammed themselves shut at night, loud enough that several residents moved out rather than endure it. The disturbances didn't stop until the stone was eventually hauled back to its original spot in the yard. Today, The Burgher's Home operates as a small museum - and the ghost, it turns out, still has opinions. Staff say activity flared up again after the museum's 2021 history of the house described Wickholm as "grumpy".
